sink: child_process.exec (via promisify) running /bin/sh -c with the command string built by string interpolation
guard: bypassable: multiline branch's per-line escaper (escapeAppleScriptString, lines 187-193) escapes only backslash/double-quote/tab and never a single quote, unlike the single-line branch (lines 130-144) which does escape single quotes for the outer shell
why: index.ts:76-94 passes the fully caller-controlled `command` string straight to CommandExecutor.executeCommand (no validation). When command contains a newline (line 43), it is built via prepareMultilineCommand->escapeAppleScriptString (lines 159-193), which never escapes single quotes, then embedded unquoted-for-shell inside the outer single-quoted osascript -e argument (line 46) that is passed to exec()/bin/sh -c. A command containing a newline plus a single quote (e.g. command = "a\nb'; touch /tmp/pwned #") closes the shell's outer single-quoted argument early, turning the following ';' into a real shell command separator, so 'touch /tmp/pwned' executes as an actual OS command on the host running the MCP server -- not merely typed into the iTerm session -- which exceeds the tool's advertised scope of writing text into a terminal.
